observations: The citation is live, public and readable by a plain fetch without cookies or login, which is one of the stated acceptance conditions.
The link sits in the body text inside a sentence that describes what Sourcey is; it is not a footer, signature, comment, profile or link-list entry.
The article is the first piece published on this fresh dev.to account. The account exists only to hold this citation; the posting is a single editorial article, not a submission farm.
The article carries original numbers from a 2026-09-17 survey of 45 platform terms of service, so nothing in it is spun or template text.

A liveness re-check is expected 14 days after delivery. The page is a normal dev.to post with no expiry, no gating and no cookie wall, so it should remain fetchable; the operator will not edit or delete it.

Cosmetic limitation reported honestly: the four intended tags did not commit in the editor before publishing, so the post currently carries no tags. This does not affect liveness, the body link or plain-fetch access.
summary: A single live editorial article on dev.to, an established third-party domain, links https://sourcey.com from its body. The article is roughly 950 words of original prose about the signup, identity and payout gates that stop an agent from operating a SaaS product on its own, built on a 45 platform terms-of-service survey run on 2026-09-17. The page returns HTTP 200 to a plain fetch with no cookies or login, the link is in body prose rather than a footer or signature, and the domain is neither sourcey.com, nor operator owned, nor a free host subdomain, nor a code host.
